q: An auditor of a nonissuer concludes that inventory is overstated by an amount that is material but not pervasive, and management refuses to adjust. Which opinion should be expressed?
choices: Qualified opinion
Adverse opinion
Disclaimer of opinion
Unmodified opinion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
exp: Under AU-C 705, a material misstatement that is not pervasive results in a qualified ('except for') opinion. An adverse opinion requires the misstatement to be both material and pervasive, and an emphasis-of-matter paragraph cannot be used to address a misstatement.

q: In an audit report on a nonissuer's financial statements under AU-C 700, which section must appear first?
choices: Basis for Opinion
Opinion
Responsibilities of Management for the Financial Statements
Key Audit Matters
exp: AU-C 700 (as revised by SAS 134) requires the Opinion section to be presented first, followed immediately by the Basis for Opinion section. Key audit matters, when communicated, follow the Basis for Opinion and any going concern section.

q: Before accepting an engagement, the auditor learns that management will prohibit confirmation of receivables and observation of inventory, both of which are material and whose possible effects would be pervasive. No law requires the auditor to accept. What should the auditor do?
choices: Accept and issue a qualified opinion
Accept and issue an adverse opinion
Decline the engagement
Accept and perform alternative procedures, then issue an unmodified opinion
exp: AU-C 210 and AU-C 705 indicate that if management imposes a scope limitation before acceptance that would likely result in a disclaimer, the auditor should not accept the engagement unless required by law or regulation. An adverse opinion addresses misstatements, not scope limitations.

q: An auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence about a foreign subsidiary's balances, and the possible effects of undetected misstatements are both material and pervasive. The auditor should express:
choices: A qualified opinion
An adverse opinion
An unmodified opinion with an other-matter paragraph
A disclaimer of opinion
exp: AU-C 705 requires a disclaimer when the auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate evidence and the possible effects could be both material and pervasive. An adverse opinion is reserved for misstatements the auditor has actually concluded exist.

q: When the auditor disclaims an opinion on a nonissuer's financial statements, which change to the report is required?
choices: The report omits the statement that the auditor believes the evidence obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for an opinion
The report includes a Key Audit Matters section describing the scope limitation
The report expresses an opinion on the components that were audited
The report is dated as of the original planned completion date
exp: In a disclaimer, the basis section is retitled 'Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion' and the statement that evidence is sufficient and appropriate is omitted (AU-C 705). Piecemeal opinions on components are not permitted when disclaiming on the financial statements as a whole, and KAMs are not communicated.

q: A nonissuer client changes from FIFO to weighted-average cost for inventory, the change is justified and properly accounted for and disclosed, and its effect is material. How should the auditor's report be affected?
choices: Qualified opinion for lack of consistency
Unmodified opinion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph describing the change in accounting principle
No reference to the change is required
Unmodified opinion with an other-matter paragraph
exp: AU-C 708 requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph when there is a change in accounting principle that has a material effect, even when the change is justified. A qualified opinion would be appropriate only if the change were not in accordance with the framework.

q: An auditor concludes that substantial doubt about a nonissuer's ability to continue as a going concern exists and management's disclosures are adequate. Under AU-C 570, the auditor's report should:
choices: Include a qualified opinion
Include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph titled 'Going Concern'
Include a separate section with the heading 'Substantial Doubt About the Entity's Ability to Continue as a Going Concern'
Include an adverse opinion
exp: AU-C 570 (SAS 132) requires a separate section with that specific heading when substantial doubt exists and disclosures are adequate; the opinion is unmodified. A modified opinion is appropriate only when disclosure is inadequate or the going concern basis is inappropriate.

q: Which of the following matters would most likely be included in an other-matter paragraph rather than an emphasis-of-matter paragraph?
choices: A major catastrophe that has had a significant effect on the entity's financial position, appropriately disclosed
Significant uncertainty about the outcome of litigation, appropriately disclosed
An early application of a new accounting standard with a material effect
The prior-period financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor whose report is not reissued
exp: An other-matter paragraph addresses matters not presented or disclosed in the financial statements that are relevant to users' understanding of the audit or the report, such as a predecessor auditor's prior-year report (AU-C 706/700). The other items are disclosed matters fundamental to users' understanding, which are emphasis-of-matter subjects.

q: For an audit of a large accelerated filer under PCAOB AS 3101, which of the following is required in the auditor's report?
choices: Communication of critical audit matters, or a statement that there are none
A section describing key audit matters under AU-C 701
An emphasis-of-matter paragraph for every significant estimate
A statement of the audit fee
exp: AS 3101 requires communication of critical audit matters in audits of issuers other than excluded entities (such as EGCs and brokers/dealers), or a statement that the auditor determined there are none. Key audit matters under AU-C 701 apply only when a nonissuer auditor is engaged to communicate them.

q: Which of the following is required in an auditor's report on an issuer's financial statements under PCAOB AS 3101 but is not required in a report under AU-C 700?
choices: A statement that the audit was conducted in accordance with applicable auditing standards
A statement of the year in which the auditor began serving consecutively as the company's auditor
Identification of the financial statements audited
An opinion on whether the financial statements are presented fairly in all material respects
exp: AS 3101 requires a statement of auditor tenure. Both frameworks require a statement about the auditing standards, identification of the statements, and the opinion.

q: An auditor of a nonissuer is engaged to communicate key audit matters. The auditor issues a qualified opinion due to a misstatement of goodwill. How should the goodwill matter be handled?
choices: Describe it in the Key Audit Matters section instead of the Basis for Qualified Opinion section
Describe it in both the Key Audit Matters section and an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
Describe it in the Basis for Qualified Opinion section and refer to that section in the Key Audit Matters section rather than describing it as a KAM
Omit it from the report because it is already reflected in the opinion
exp: AU-C 701 states that a matter giving rise to a modified opinion is by nature a key audit matter but is not described in the KAM section; instead the KAM section refers to the basis for qualified opinion section. Communicating a KAM is never a substitute for a modified opinion.

q: An auditor's report on a nonissuer is dated March 10. On March 20, before the report is released, a subsequent event requiring disclosure occurs and is disclosed by management. The auditor performs procedures only on that event. The auditor should:
choices: Redate the report to March 20 without performing additional procedures
Leave the report dated March 10 with no reference to the event
Issue a separate report on the subsequent event
Dual-date the report, for example 'March 10, except for Note X, as to which the date is March 20'
exp: AU-C 560 permits dual dating so that the auditor's responsibility for events after the original date is limited to the specific note. Redating the entire report extends responsibility to all subsequent events and requires procedures through the new date.

q: An auditor's report on comparative financial statements includes an updated opinion on the prior period that differs from the opinion previously expressed. Under AU-C 700, the auditor should:
choices: Disclose in an other-matter paragraph the date and type of the previous opinion, the reasons for the different opinion, and that the updated opinion differs
Issue an adverse opinion on the current period
Omit the prior period from the report
Include the matter only in the management letter
exp: When an updated opinion on prior-period statements differs from the previous opinion, the auditor discloses the reasons in an other-matter paragraph, including the date and type of prior opinion. The current period's opinion is unaffected unless the matter also affects it.

q: A nonissuer omits from its financial statements a disclosure required by GAAP that is material but not pervasive. If practicable, the auditor's report should:
choices: Express an adverse opinion and omit the information
Express a qualified opinion and include the omitted information in the basis for qualified opinion section
Express an unmodified opinion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph containing the information
Express a disclaimer of opinion
exp: AU-C 705 requires that for omitted required disclosures, the auditor describes the nature of the omitted information and, if practicable and the information is available, includes it in the basis paragraph. The opinion is qualified when material but not pervasive.

q: Required supplementary information (RSI) accompanies a nonissuer's audited financial statements and the auditor applied the limited procedures with no exceptions. The auditor's report should include:
choices: An opinion on the RSI in relation to the financial statements as a whole
No reference to RSI
An other-matter paragraph referring to the RSI and stating that limited procedures were applied and no opinion is expressed
An emphasis-of-matter paragraph stating the RSI is fairly presented
exp: AU-C 730 requires an other-matter paragraph addressing RSI in all cases, stating the limited procedures and that the auditor does not express an opinion. An 'in relation to' opinion applies to supplementary information under AU-C 725, not to RSI.

q: A nonissuer's annual report contains other information (a letter to shareholders) that the auditor obtained before the report date. The auditor read it and found no material inconsistency. Under AU-C 720, the report should:
choices: Contain an opinion on the other information
Omit any reference to the other information
Include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph on the other information
Include a separate section titled 'Other Information' describing management's responsibility and the auditor's responsibility and conclusion
exp: AU-C 720 (SAS 137) requires a separate 'Other Information' section when the annual report contains other information, stating that the auditor does not express an opinion on it and describing the result of reading it. No opinion is expressed on other information.

q: An auditor of a nonissuer audits financial statements prepared on the cash basis of accounting. Under AU-C 800, the auditor's report should include:
choices: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph alerting users to the basis of accounting and stating that it is a basis other than GAAP
An adverse opinion because the statements depart from GAAP
A restriction on use paragraph for all cash basis reports
A qualified opinion
exp: AU-C 800 requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph that refers to the note describing the special purpose framework. Restricted use is required for contractual and regulatory bases, not for cash or tax basis, and no modification is needed because GAAP is not the applicable framework.

q: Which of the following is the correct date for an auditor's report on a nonissuer?
choices: The date the auditor began fieldwork

No earlier than the date on which the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate evidence, including evidence that the financial statements were prepared and that those with authority have asserted responsibility for them
The date of the balance sheet
The date the financial statements are issued to users
exp: AU-C 700 requires the report to be dated no earlier than when sufficient appropriate evidence is obtained, including evidence that the statements, including disclosures, have been prepared and management has asserted responsibility. Issuance may occur later than the report date.

q: An auditor concludes that a nonissuer failed to consolidate a material subsidiary, and the effects are both material and pervasive. The auditor should express:
choices: A qualified opinion
A disclaimer of opinion
An adverse opinion
An unmodified opinion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
exp: A material and pervasive misstatement, such as failure to consolidate, results in an adverse opinion under AU-C 705. A disclaimer is for scope limitations, and a qualified opinion is for misstatements that are not pervasive.

q: In an adverse opinion on a nonissuer's financial statements, the auditor's report should:
choices: Express an unmodified opinion on the balance sheet and adverse opinion on the income statement as piecemeal opinions
Omit the basis section
State that the auditor was unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence
Include a 'Basis for Adverse Opinion' section describing the matter and, if practicable, quantifying its effects
exp: AU-C 705 requires a Basis for Adverse Opinion section describing and quantifying the misstatement if practicable. Piecemeal opinions are not permitted with an adverse opinion on the statements as a whole, and inability to obtain evidence relates to disclaimers.

q: The auditor of a nonissuer is also engaged to report on supplementary schedules of operating expenses accompanying the financial statements. Under AU-C 725, the auditor's report on the schedules most typically states that:
choices: The information is fairly stated, in all material respects, in relation to the financial statements as a whole
The information is presented fairly in accordance with GAAP as a standalone statement
The auditor applied limited procedures and expresses no opinion
The information was compiled from management's records
exp: Under AU-C 725, the auditor reports whether supplementary information is fairly stated in relation to the financial statements as a whole. Limited procedures and no opinion describe RSI under AU-C 730.

q: A nonissuer's prior-year financial statements were restated to correct a material misstatement, and the restatement is properly disclosed. In the current-year report on comparative statements, the auditor should:
choices: Issue a qualified opinion on the prior year
Include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph regarding the correction of the misstatement
Make no reference to the restatement
Issue a disclaimer on the prior year
exp: AU-C 708 requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph for a correction of a material misstatement in previously issued financial statements. The restated statements are fairly presented, so no qualification is needed.

q: Under AU-C 705, the term 'pervasive' describes effects on the financial statements that:
choices: Exceed overall materiality by any amount
Relate to a single account balance that is large
Are not confined to specific elements, or if confined represent a substantial proportion of the statements, or relate to disclosures fundamental to users' understanding
Relate to fraud involving senior management
exp: AU-C 705 defines pervasive effects as those not confined to specific elements, accounts, or items, or if confined, representing a substantial proportion of the statements, or disclosures fundamental to understanding. Exceeding materiality alone makes something material, not pervasive.

q: An auditor of a nonissuer identifies a matter that is appropriately disclosed and is of such importance that it is fundamental to users' understanding of the financial statements. The auditor is not engaged to report KAMs. The auditor may:
choices: Qualify the opinion
Disclose additional facts not included in the financial statements
Include an other-matter paragraph
Include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph that refers only to information presented or disclosed in the financial statements
exp: AU-C 706 permits an emphasis-of-matter paragraph for appropriately disclosed matters fundamental to users' understanding, and it may refer only to information presented or disclosed. The auditor does not provide original information about the entity, and no qualification applies when no misstatement exists.

q: A nonissuer prepares financial statements in accordance with a contractual basis of accounting for use by a lender. Under AU-C 800, which is required?
choices: An other-matter paragraph restricting the use of the report to the specified parties
An adverse opinion for departure from GAAP
A disclaimer of opinion
A statement that the financial statements comply with GAAP
exp: AU-C 800 requires a restricted-use alert in an other-matter paragraph when statements are prepared under a contractual or regulatory basis of accounting. Special purpose frameworks are not departures from GAAP requiring modification.

q: An auditor of a nonissuer engaged to communicate KAMs determines that a significant matter is fundamental to users' understanding and is also a KAM. Which is most appropriate?
choices: Include it as both an emphasis-of-matter paragraph and a KAM, repeating the same text
Communicate it in the KAM section, which may highlight its relative importance, rather than also in an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
Exclude it from the report entirely
Qualify the opinion on the matter
exp: AU-C 706 states that an emphasis-of-matter paragraph is not a substitute for a KAM, and when a matter is determined to be a KAM, the auditor generally communicates it in the KAM section rather than in a separate emphasis-of-matter paragraph. No qualification is warranted for an appropriately presented matter.

q: When a predecessor auditor's report on prior-period comparative statements is not reissued, the successor auditor's report should include an other-matter paragraph stating:
choices: That the successor reaudited the prior period
The name of the predecessor auditor in all cases
That the prior-period statements were audited by another auditor, the type of opinion and date of that report, and the reasons for any modification
That the successor assumes responsibility for the predecessor's work
exp: AU-C 700 requires an other-matter paragraph indicating that a predecessor audited the prior period, the date and type of opinion, and reasons for any modification. The predecessor is generally not named, and the successor does not assume responsibility for the predecessor's work.

q: A nonissuer auditor issues a qualified opinion due to an inability to observe beginning inventory. Which wording is consistent with the qualified opinion?
choices: 'Because of the significance of the matter, we do not express an opinion'
'The financial statements do not present fairly'
'Except for the effects of the matter described in the Basis for Qualified Opinion section, the financial statements present fairly...'
'Except for the possible effects of the matter described in the Basis for Qualified Opinion section, the financial statements present fairly...'
exp: When qualifying due to a scope limitation, AU-C 705 uses 'except for the possible effects,' because the auditor has not determined that a misstatement exists. 'Except for the effects' is used for actual misstatements.

q: An auditor of a nonissuer becomes aware, after the report date but before release, that management materially revised a disclosure. Which is most appropriate?
choices: Extend subsequent-event procedures to the new date and either dual-date or redate the report as applicable
Release the report with the original date and no further procedures
Withdraw from the engagement
Issue an adverse opinion
exp: When financial statements are amended after the report date, AU-C 560 requires the auditor to perform procedures on the amendment and either dual-date (limiting procedures to the amendment) or redate the report (extending procedures). Releasing without considering the change is inappropriate.

q: An auditor's report on a nonissuer includes an emphasis-of-matter paragraph. Which statement about that paragraph is accurate?
choices: It modifies the auditor's opinion
It must include a statement that the auditor's opinion is not modified with respect to the matter
It is used to describe misstatements that management refused to correct
It must be placed before the Opinion section
exp: AU-C 706 requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph to state that the opinion is not modified with respect to the matter emphasized. It is not a modification, and misstatements require a modified opinion.
